system:
You read documents filed on a United States court docket, OCR'd to markdown, for
a research dataset of contract clauses.

An INSTRUMENT is a document whose text the parties negotiated and by which they
bound each other: a contract, agreement, policy, lease, deed, guaranty, note,
plan, bylaws, handbook, amendment, or similar. Hallmarks: recitals, defined
terms, numbered operative sections, an execution or signature block.

A FILING is a document made for the court: complaint, answer, motion, brief,
memorandum, order, affidavit, declaration, notice, docket sheet, certificate of
service, civil cover sheet.

THE DECISIVE RULE. A filing that **attaches** an instrument counts — report the
instrument's own boundaries, not the filing's. A filing that merely **quotes** an
instrument does not count at all: a brief reproducing three sentences of an
agreement is a filing, and the file contains no instrument.

WHAT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT, even when signed or filled in: a blank or fill-in
form; an agency certificate or registration; an exhibit index; a declarations
page or coverage-summary table; a schedule of rates or fees standing alone; an
invoice, receipt or statement of account. These record or summarise; the parties
did not negotiate their text.

WHAT IS NOT A PROVISION: a heading on its own; a title page; a table of
contents; a signature, notary or attestation block; an exhibit index. A
provision states an obligation, right, grant, limitation, condition or
definition. Give the range of the operative text, including its heading.

LIST EVERY SUBSTANTIVE PROVISION, in document order. Do not skip any. Do not
judge whether a provision is well or badly drafted. Do not rank them.

The file is given to you with a line number and a `│` at the start of every line.
Line numbers are not part of the text; they are how you point at it.

OCR REPAIR. For each provision you must also give its text. Copy it verbatim
from the lines you named, then repair only what the scanner broke: words split
across a line break, words run together, `l`/`1` and `O`/`0` confusions, stray
table pipes and cell debris, page numbers and Bates stamps sitting inside the
text. Do not paraphrase, modernise, reorder, summarise, or drop anything. Never
change a number, an amount, a date, or a cross-reference. Never add or remove a
word — a repair that deletes `not` inverts the clause. If a passage is too
damaged to repair honestly, copy it as it stands.

Add nothing of your own: no `[struck through: ...]`, no `[sic]`, no
`[illegible]`, no explanatory brackets of any kind. Executed contracts are often
marked up by hand, and the OCR shows deleted wording as `~~struck~~`. Reproduce
those words as plain text, in place, and say what you saw in the repairs
sentence instead.

   11│## MERITER HEALTH SERVICES, INC. BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING
   12│
   13│DATE: August 28, 2002
   14│
   15│PRESENT: Howard Bellman, Jeff Bartell, Phil Blake, Jac Garner, Judy Householder, Sandy Kamnetz, M.D., Brad Manning, M.D., Regina Millner, Tom Olson, Paul Percy, Ph.D., John Pollock, Terri Potter, Betsy Trowbridge, M.D., Charles Weber, M.D., Gary Wolter
   16│
   17│ABSENT: Gloria Jones-Bey
   18│
   19│ALSO PRESENT: Robert Coats, Tom Fuss, Pauline Harrop, William Morgan, Charles Possin, Geoff Priest, M.D., Tim Sio, Carl Weston, M.D.
   20│
   21│### **EDUCATION**
   22│
   23│During the education session, Mr. Coats, MHS Senior Vice President, presented the results of the "Portfolio Assessment - Phase 2."
   24│
   25│### **CALL TO ORDER**
   26│
   27│The meeting was called to order by Ms. Millner, Chair, at 5:35 p.m. in the Tower A Conference Room at Meriter Hospital-Park.
   28│
   29│### **MINUTES**
   30│
   31│A motion was made, seconded and carried to approve the minutes of the June 26, 2002 meeting as presented.
   32│
   33│### **CODE OF ETHICS POLICY**
   34│
   35│Ms. Millner presented the Meriter Code of Ethics for the scheduled biennial review by the Board. No changes were proposed.
   36│
   37│A motion was made, seconded and carried to approve the Meriter Code of Ethics with no changes from the current version.
   38│
   39│### **ELECTIONS AND COMMITTEE APPOINTMENTS**
   40│
   41│#### **Meriter Retirement Services Board of Directors**
   42│
   43│On behalf of the Nominating Committee, Ms. Householder forwarded the nomination of Mr. Eric Stanchfield to the Meriter Retirement Services Board of Directors.
   44│
   45│A motion was made to elect Eric Stanchfield to the Class of 2005 of the Meriter Retirement Services Board of Directors. It was seconded and carried.
   46│
   47│Meriter Health Services, Inc.  
   48│Board Meeting – August 28, 2002
   49│
   50│2
   51│
   52│#### MHS/MH/MMS Boards of Directors
   53│
   54│Mr. Tom Zimbrick was nominated for election to the Meriter Health Services, Meriter Hospital and Meriter Management Services Boards of Directors.
   55│
   56│It was moved, seconded and carried to adopt the following resolution.
   57│
   58│**RESOLVED**, by the Board of Directors of Meriter Health Services, Inc., as the Sole Voting Member of Meriter Hospital, Inc. and the Sole Shareholder of Meriter Management Services, Inc., that we hereby elect Tom Zimbrick to the Class of 2004 of the Boards of Directors of Meriter Hospital and Meriter Management Services, effective immediately; and
   59│
   60│**FURTHER RESOLVED**, that we hereby authorize and direct the President of Meriter Health Services, Inc. to cast the vote on behalf of the MHS Board in accordance with the preceding resolution; and
   61│
   62│**FURTHER RESOLVED**, that Tom Zimbrick be and hereby is elected as a director of Meriter Health Services, Inc., to a term which is effective August 28, 2002, and which expires at the annual meeting in 2004.
   63│
   64│#### Committee Appointment
   65│
   66│Ms. Millner recommended committee appointments for Mr. Zimbrick.
   67│
   68│**A motion was made, seconded and carried to appoint Tom Zimbrick to the MHS Public Service Committee, effective immediately.**
   69│
   70│The Board was informed that Mr. Zimbrick will also serve on the Hospital's Personnel Committee.
   71│
   72│### PORTFOLIO ASSESSMENT
   73│
   74│During the education session of the meeting, Mr. Coats explained that work on Phase 1 of the Meriter Portfolio Assessment, which encompassed the Hospital along with selected corporate services, was concluded by the Board on August 29, 2001. A brief update on the implementation of initiatives resulting from Phase 1 was provided to the Board. Mr. Coats then reported the results of Phase 2, an assessment of the other components of the Meriter system which was undertaken in 2002. The Board reviewed the aim and scope of the project, driving forces and the decision criteria. The resolution on the Portfolio Assessment-Phase 2 was presented for consideration.
   75│
   76│**A motion was made, seconded and carried to adopt the following resolution.**
   77│
   78│**WHEREAS**, management has completed Phase 2 of the comprehensive assessment of Meriter's portfolio of services, designed to determine whether any modifications are required in order to improve the profitability of the Meriter system, to support patient outcomes, to increase customer satisfaction, or to support Meriter's mission of community services; and
   79│
   80│**WHEREAS, the MHS Board has reviewed the portfolio decisions made by management and the recommendations to be submitted to subsidiary boards of directors;**
   81│
   82│**NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the MHS Board of Directors hereby ratifies the portfolio decisions made by management with respect to the Sales Department and Corporate Finance Division and further ratifies the portfolio recommendations to be forwarded to the Boards of Directors of Meriter Health Enterprises and Meriter Retirement Services for action.**
   83│
   84│### **REAL ESTATE AND FACILITY PLANNING**
   85│
   86│The report of the ad hoc Real Estate Committee was presented by Mr. Wolter. He summarized the work conducted on siting the Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Program. The option of relocating the Program from the Capitol to the Park Campus was determined not to be conducive to the care and treatment of this patient population. Potential off-site locations were assessed, which led to identification of Meriter's Raymond Road property as the preferred site.
   87│
   88│Mr. Coats reviewed the features of the Raymond Road site plan. Precise location and design of a new facility are yet to be determined. The timeline was explained. Mr. Coats noted it is an aggressive timeline designed to vacate the Capitol Campus by the end of 2003. Next steps include: communication with internal Meriter audiences and external publics, clarification of project scope and completion of the capital budget, City review and approval process, and annexation and zoning approvals. The Board suggested communicating with UW Hospital and St. Marys to gain their public support and recognition for this critical community service to be sustained by Meriter. Communications with the Raymond Road neighborhood, with political leaders and the alderperson were discussed also. He responded to questions about the rationale for annexation, prospects for use of the former NewStart CBRF facility, and potential uses of the excess property not occupied by the Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Program.
   89│
   90│### **MAINGATE**
   91│
   92│Ms. Millner reminded the Board that in June the MHS Executive Committee was authorized to approve modifications to the MainGate project business model. Those modifications, as approved at the July 11, 2002 joint meeting of the Executive Committees of MHS and Meriter Retirement Services, were presented to the Board.
   93│
   94│**Attached to the permanent minutes is a copy of the resolution adopted by the MHS Executive Committee.**
   95│
   96│Mr. Possin provided an update on the project: \$4 million has been raised through the "Grow Among Friends" capital campaign; 37% of the apartment homes have been sold; and construction contracts are close to being finalized. He announced that a groundbreaking ceremony is scheduled for September 18.
   97│
   98│Meriter Health Services, Inc.  
   99│Board Meeting – August 28, 2002
  100│
  101│4
  102│
  103│### **PENSION PLAN REDESIGN**
  104│
  105│Mr. Pollock introduced the Pension Plan redesign project. He explained the issues that require Meriter to redesign its pension plan and described the main features of the proposed design, as well as the alternatives considered. The transition plan was outlined. Mr. Pollock specifically noted that employees age 60 years or older will be grandfathered into the new plan, with retirement benefits calculated using the existing plan formula. This is deemed necessary in order that employees near retirement are not harmed by the change. In response to questions, Mr. Morgan informed the Board that both unions have ratified the proposed plan changes. A resolution was introduced.
  106│
  107│**A motion was made, seconded and carried to adopt the following resolution.**
  108│
  109│**BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED** by the Board of Directors of Meriter Health Services, Inc. that this Corporation accepts the recommendation of the Executive Compensation and Pension Committee regarding revisions to the Meriter Health Services Employee Retirement Plan and the Meriter Health Services Employees' Long-Range Savings Plan (the "Retirement Plans"); and
  110│
  111│**FURTHER RESOLVED** that the officers of this Corporation be and hereby are authorized and directed to amend and restate the Retirement Plans as necessary and appropriate to implement the recommendations of the Executive Compensation and Pension Committee; and
  112│
  113│**FURTHER RESOLVED** that the amended and restated Retirement Plans be filed with the Internal Revenue Service for determination letters as to their qualified status under the provisions of the Internal Revenue Code; and
  114│
  115│**FURTHER RESOLVED** that copies of the amended and restated Retirement Plans, when fully executed and approved by the Internal Revenue Service, shall be kept on file in the office of the Corporation.
  116│
  117│### **AUDIT COMMITTEE**
  118│
  119│The report of the Audit Committee was provided to the Board. An ad hoc subcommittee has conducted an assessment of the Committee's function and operations. Report modifications have been made and have been well received by Committee members. The Audit Committee has also discussed how it discharges its audit responsibilities on audit and control questions given the current environment nationwide.
  120│
  121│Mr. Fuss reported that Meriter's executive team met with the rating agencies, Standard & Poor's and Moody's, in mid-August. Although final determinations have not yet been received, preliminary responses have indicated the rating teams will be recommending that Meriter retain its "A" bond rating.
  122│
  123│Meriter Health Services, Inc.  
  124│Board Meeting – August 28, 2002
  125│
  126│5
  127│
  128│### MANAGEMENT REPORT
  129│
  130│Mr. Potter and Mr. Coats highlighted selected items from the August Management Report.
  131│
  132│*UW Health Relations* – Meriter has reached verbal agreement on the Hospitalist arrangement and has also reached verbal agreement on the Breast Health Collaborative effort. Negotiations with the UW regarding the Perinatal and Neonatal programs are continuing.
  133│
  134│*Legal Counsel* – A recommendation regarding legal counsel to serve Meriter on health law matters will be presented to the Board at the September meeting.
  135│
  136│### *PPIC*
  137│
  138│- > Opening of the State bids revealed Group Health Cooperative and Unity came in much lower than expected. The Board discussed the implications for PPIC, the business risks, and the sales and marketing implications.
  139│- > A \$2.5 million advance payment on Meriter's surplus note was received today from PPIC.
  140│- > Finalists for the PPIC Sales and Marketing executive are being interviewed.
  141│- > Two new products will be introduced this fall: Basic Care to meet the needs of the small employer and a replacement product for mid-size businesses that have multiple plans.
  142│
  143│*Good News Stories* – Meriter is continuing to publish its "Good News" stories. Examples were shared with the Board.
  144│
  145│*Board Recognition* – On September 29, Meriter will be publishing an ad in the Wisconsin State Journal recognizing community leaders who serve on the Meriter boards of directors.
  146│
  147│*Employee Recognition* – Meriter's Employee Recognition Event is scheduled on September 5. Board members were encouraged to attend.
  148│
  149│*Board Education* – Conferences sponsored by the Governance Institute were highlighted. Board members were encouraged to contact Mr. Potter and advise him of the conference(s) they would like to attend.
  150│
  151│*Quarterly Measures Report* – The Board reviewed selected performance indicators. Only one indicator is rated "yellow." Results of efforts to reduce patient falls are not as expected and this is a priority measure being monitored. Mr. Potter also reviewed data on Employee Opinion Survey results, nursing turnover and vacancy rates, accounts receivable, and the case mix index.
  152│
  153│### ADJOURNMENT
  154│
  155│There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:10 p.m.
  156│
  157│   
  158│\_\_\_\_\_  
  159│Regina Millner, Chair
  160│
  161│Recorded by: Pauline C. Harrop
  162│
  163│### JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEES OF MERITER HEALTH SERVICES, INC. AND MERITER RETIREMENT SERVICES, INC.
  164│
  165│RE: Modified Financial Model for MainGate Development Project
  166│
  167│WHEREAS, in September 2001, the MHS and MRS Boards of Directors established threshold goals for fundraising and apartment home pre-sales which were to be met prior to proceeding with the ground breaking for MainGate at Meriter Commons, and in January 2002 the Boards approved a plan of financing for the project; and
  168│
  169│WHEREAS, due primarily to the downturn in the economy, those threshold goals were not achieved by the May 1, 2002, target date, with the Capital Campaign having raised \$3,802,508 toward the \$4,000,000 threshold goal and the Sales Team having pre-sold 32% of the life lease dollar value as compared to the 50% sales target; and
  170│
  171│WHEREAS, upon further study of the market assumptions and forecast and further analysis of projections for fund raising and sales, management has determined that the project continues to be a financially viable, significant component of Meriter's senior housing development strategy; and
  172│
  173│WHEREAS, various financing scenarios which would allow construction to begin prior to achieving the threshold goals and which result in acceptable financial ratios and financial performance were reviewed by the MRS Executive and Finance Committees on June 4, 2002; and
  174│
  175│WHEREAS, management and the MRS Executive and Finance Committees also reviewed the risks of delaying the project, concluding that delay of MainGate past September 2002 will have negative implications for current donors, committed prospective residents, future pre-sales, project costs and project credibility, and also concluding that proceeding with construction will create a positive stimulus for additional donations and apartment sales; and
  176│
  177│WHEREAS, management has prepared a revised business model, financing plan and financial proforma for consideration by the Boards of Directors of Meriter Health Services and Meriter Retirement Services; and
  178│
  179│WHEREAS, the MHS Board of Directors has authorized the MHS Executive Committee to make decisions necessary to resolve any policy issues related to the MainGate project on behalf of the MHS Board of Directors and to approve a modified business model acceptable to both Meriter Health Services and Meriter Retirement Services;
  180│
  181│- continued -
  182│
  183│NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the MHS and MRS Executive Committees hereby recommend for approval by the MRS Board of Directors the modified financial model for MainGate at Meriter Commons, with a revised total project cost not to exceed \$19,023,125; and
  184│
  185│FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Executive Committees recommend that the MRS Board authorize proceeding with construction no later than September 15, 2002, with the understanding that this date may be prior to achieving the fund raising and pre-sales targets originally established for the project; and
  186│
  187│FURTHER RESOLVED, that the life lease contracts be changed to defer collection of 85% of the fees until the residential units are ready for occupancy, recognizing that this creates the need for a construction loan; and
  188│
  189│FURTHER RESOLVED, that the MHS and MRS Executive Committees recommend approval of the plan to obtain a \$7 million construction loan by issuing a two-year taxable variable rate note with USBank on terms substantially the same as those described in the materials submitted to the Committees as of this date, and
  190│
  191│FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Committees recommend the Meriter Foundation Board endorse the possibility of placing restrictions on the freedom to use Foundation funds designated for Meriter Retirement Services during the period of time the construction note is outstanding in order for MRS to preserve a minimum liquidity balance of \$5 million, the sum of which includes a combination of MRS cash, marketable securities and funds held by the Foundation ; and
  192│
  193│FURTHER RESOLVED, that in accordance with the authority granted to it in the resolution adopted by the MHS Board of Directors on June 26, 2002, the MHS Executive Committee hereby approves the modified financial model for MainGate and the plan of action to implement that model as described by the foregoing resolutions, and further authorizes and directs management to take any and all necessary steps and to execute any documents necessary to complete that plan of action, including obtaining the construction loan, with the understanding that this action of the MHS Executive Committee shall be reported to the MHS Board of Directors in August 2002.
  194│
  195│ADOPTED this 11th day of July, 2002.
